name: Pin analysis (Classic chess)
content: Find every absolute or relative pin from the authoritative board and the supplied geometric control map. A pin consists of an enemy sliding attacker (bishop, rook or queen), a pinned opposing piece on that same attacking line, and a second friendly piece behind it (protected). The attacker must control the pinned piece's square in the supplied map. Use the supplied xray records directly: attacker must have one ray with first equal to the pinned piece's SQUARE and second equal to the protected piece's SQUARE. Do not rediscover rays from board or infer a relation missing from xray. The Grounder has already recorded the first and second blockers on each ray. Rooks use ranks/files; bishops diagonals; queens both. Absolute: protected is king. Relative: protected is strictly more valuable than pinned under P=1, N=3, B=3, R=5, Q=9. Compare the two protected-side pieces, NOT the value of the attacker. Exclude skewers (valuable piece in front), equal-value relative obstructions, x-rays with extra blockers, and moves/evaluation. A pinned piece may still move along the ray: do not assume immobilization. Use only real IDs supplied by the map. Include each unique pin exactly once and sort by pinned, attacker, protected. You may reason in prose before the final result. End your response with a single JSON object (optionally in a Markdown json fence) and nothing afterwards: {"version":1,"pins":[{"attacker":"bQ_d8","pinned":"wN_d5","protected":"wQ_d1","type":"relative"}]}. Example is only illustrative and MUST NOT be copied unless accurate. If there are none return {"version":1,"pins":[]}. No other fields.
